L01.name: Molten Wave Oval Ring
L01.note: it is the owner's photo of the ring worn on a finger, with a tray of other rings blurred behind: take ONLY the ring on the finger and ignore the tray and every ring in it. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the same ring.
L01.lock: AN OPEN WRAP RING OF THREE MOLTEN GOLD STRANDS: three smooth, slightly irregular, high-polish gold strands, like poured liquid gold, sweep side by side across the top of the finger and fan apart. The outer strand is the thickest, about 2.5mm, swelling into a rounded droplet at its end; the middle strand is slimmer, about 1.5mm; the third, fine strand bends around ONE OVAL clear faceted stone held in four slim gold claws, so the oval sits at the front of the ring beside the strands, its long axis along the strands. The strands look hand-poured, with soft ripples, never machined.
L01.neg: Exactly one stone: one clear oval, never round, never pear; no pave, no halo, no other stones anywhere; the strands are smooth polished gold, never twisted rope, never textured; exactly three strands, never two, never four.
L01.scale: The oval stone is about 6x8mm, smaller than a fingernail; the strands are 1.5 to 2.5mm wide; at its widest the ring covers about 15mm.
L01.wscale: On the finger the ring covers about 15mm of the finger, never wider than the finger, and the oval stone is about a third of the finger's width.
L01.place: standing upright on the top face, the oval stone and the three strands facing the camera
L01.macro: the oval stone in its four claws and the three molten strands sweeping beside it

L02.name: Marquise Molten Bar Ring
L02.note: it is the owner's photo of the ring worn on a finger, with a tray of other rings blurred behind: take ONLY the ring on the finger. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the same ring.
L02.lock: AN OPEN TOI-ET-MOI RING with a BOLD, WEIGHTY look, exactly as IMAGE 1 shows: a polished gold band that does NOT close, its two open ends side by side on top of the finger, both running in the same direction as the band. At one end ONE LARGE clear MARQUISE-cut faceted stone, about 5.5 x 11mm, in four strong gold claws, its long axis following the band. The band's other end becomes ONE long, CHUNKY molten gold BAR: a solid, glossy, organic rod, gently wavy like poured metal, about 2mm thick along its length and swelling to rounded droplet ends about 3mm across, about 25mm long. The bar is THICK: about a third of the marquise's width, a bold rod that carries one long bright highlight down its length. The marquise sits beside the lower half of the bar, and the bar's upper half rises well past the marquise's tip. The marquise and the bar lie side by side and parallel, both in line with the band; on the finger both lie ACROSS the finger.
L02.neg: Exactly one stone, a clear marquise, never round, oval or pear; no pave, no halo; the bar is smooth polished gold with soft ripples, never a straight machined bar, never thin like a wire, never set with stones; the band does not close. The band NEVER crosses behind the marquise and the bar at right angles: never a cross or plus shape.
L02.scale: The marquise is about 5.5 x 11mm; the molten bar is about 25mm long, a little more than twice the marquise's length, and about 2mm thick, a third of the marquise's width, its droplet ends about 3mm across.
L02.wscale: On the finger the marquise is about two thirds of the finger's width long; the bar is about one and a half finger widths long, running across the ring finger and on over the neighbouring finger, and about a tenth of the finger's width thick: a bold rod, never a wire. Never larger than this.
L02.place: standing upright on the top face, seen from the front and a little above: the marquise and the chunky molten bar stand upright side by side, the bar rising high above the marquise's tip, and from each of them the band runs straight on DOWN in the same line and curves away behind into the loop of the ring, so the loop is seen edge-on as a narrow upright oval; nothing runs left to right behind them
L02.macro: the clear marquise in its four strong claws beside the CHUNKY molten gold bar, the two parallel, the bar's full thickness and its glossy rounded droplet end clearly shown
L02.where: worn on the RING finger only, the fourth finger from the thumb, beside the little finger. ORIENTATION TEST: the ring finger points straight UP the frame, and the marquise's long axis and the molten bar BOTH lie HORIZONTALLY, LEFT TO RIGHT, at right angles to the finger, like two rungs of a ladder across it, side by side and parallel to each other; the bar's one end lies over the neighbouring finger and its other end just past the ring finger's other edge; neither ever points along the finger toward the fingertip or the knuckle

L03.name: Twin Cluster Open Ring
L03.note: it is a frame from the owner's video of the ring worn on a finger over a tray of rings: take ONLY the ring on the finger. IMAGE 2 shows the same ring design from above, several of them lying in the tray.
L03.lock: AN OPEN CLUSTER RING with a BROAD, HEAVY polished gold band, about 5 to 6mm wide and about 2mm thick, solid and chunky like a wide cigar band, exactly as IMAGE 1 and IMAGE 2 show, that does NOT close. Each open end is squared off and rises into a thick gold block that carries a small cluster of clear faceted stones in raised gold claws; the two clusters face each other across a narrow gap. One end carries exactly TWO stones: ONE clear PEAR, the larger, and ONE SMALLER clear ROUND, lined up end to end. The other end carries exactly TWO stones: two clear PEARS of the same size side by side, their rounded ends together and their points turned outward, with a row of tiny gold beads along the edge of the band beside them and nothing else. All stones clear.
L03.neg: Only clear stones: one pear and one round on one end, two pears on the other; never coloured stones, never a full pave band, never a closed band. Exactly FOUR stones in all: three pears and one small round; never five stones, never four pears, never two rounds. The end with the round has one round and one pear, never two rounds; the end with the two pears has no third stone, not even a small one.
L03.scale: Each cluster is about 10 to 12mm across: the pears about 5x7mm, the round about 4mm; the band is about 5 to 6mm wide, nearly as wide as a pear is long, and about 2mm thick.
L03.wscale: On the finger the two clusters sit SIDE BY SIDE across the top of the finger, one toward each side of it, facing each other over a narrow gap that runs ALONG the finger; in each cluster the two stones line up along the finger, one nearer the knuckle and one nearer the nail; never one cluster in front of the other along the finger; each cluster about two thirds of the finger's width long, never wider than the finger. The broad band is about a third of the finger's width wide, a solid gold band, never a thin wire.
L03.place: standing upright on the top face, the two clusters facing the camera across the opening, the broad, heavy band's width and thickness clearly visible as it curves away behind
L03.macro: the two clusters facing each other on the broad, heavy gold band: the pear and the round on one end, the two pears with their points turned outward on the other, the thick gold blocks under them and the row of tiny gold beads
L03.where: worn on the RING FINGER only (the fourth finger), the two clusters side by side across the top of the finger, one toward each side, facing each other over a narrow gap that runs along the finger: one cluster a clear PEAR beside a clear ROUND stone, the other two clear PEARS side by side with a row of tiny gold beads beside them, exactly as IMAGE 1 shows

L04.name: Lilac Flutter Studs
L04.note: it is the owner's photo of one stud on a white display ear held in a hand: take ONLY the stud; ignore the display ear, the hand and the ring on its finger. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the same stud.
L04.lock: A PAIR OF FOUR-STONE BUTTERFLY STUDS: each stud is FOUR faceted pale LILAC stones (a soft pale lavender with a hint of pink and bright white sparkle, never deep purple) in fine gold claws, set like butterfly wings around ONE tiny round gold bead at the centre: upper left a slim MARQUISE; upper right a SMALLER, SLIMMER MARQUISE, about three quarters the length of the upper-left one; lower left and lower right two larger PEARS, their points toward the centre and their round ends outward. A single post behind the centre.
L04.neg: Exactly four stones per stud, all the same pale lilac; never pink, never blue, never clear; no pave, no halo, no outline frame; the centre is one tiny gold bead; never more than one stud per ear.
L04.scale: Each stud is about 15mm across: the lower pears about 6x7mm, the marquise about 4x8mm, the smaller upper-right marquise about 3x6mm; an earlobe is about 18mm.
L04.wscale: On the lobe the stud covers most of the lobe, about 15mm, never larger than the lobe.
L04.place: both studs lying flat side by side on the top face, the stones facing up
L04.macro: ONE stud: its four lilac stones in their gold claws around the tiny gold bead

L05.name: Blush Octagon Studs
L05.note: it is the owner's photo of one stud on a white display ear held between finger and thumb: take ONLY the stud; ignore the display ear and the hand. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the same stud.
L05.lock: A PAIR OF OCTAGON SOLITAIRE STUDS: each stud is ONE OCTAGON-cut faceted stone, a REGULAR octagon with eight EQUAL straight sides (the four diagonal sides as long as the four straight ones), so it reads almost round, in a soft BLUSH PINK with peachy flashes, held in a slim gold setting with fine claws at its corners, on a single post.
L05.neg: Exactly one stone per stud; a regular octagon with eight equal sides, never a square with small clipped corners, never Asscher, never round, never a hexagon; soft blush pink, never hot pink, never red, never lilac; no halo, no pave.
L05.scale: Each stone is about 9.5mm across, about half an earlobe.
L05.wscale: On the lobe the stud is about 9.5mm across, about half the lobe's width, never larger.
L05.place: both studs lying flat side by side on the top face, the octagon tables facing up; each stone's outline is a REGULAR octagon like a stop sign, its eight sides equal, so it reads almost round
L05.macro: ONE stud: the blush octagon stone and its fine gold claws; the stone's outline a REGULAR octagon like a STOP sign, its four diagonal sides exactly as long as its four straight sides, so it reads almost round, never a square with clipped corners

L06.name: Baroque Pearl Duet Ring
L06.note: it is a close, soft crop of the ring on a finger: take ONLY the ring; it is a low-resolution image, so draw the pearl and the gold cleanly and sharply.
L06.lock: AN OPEN TOI-ET-MOI RING: a slim polished gold band that does NOT close. At one end ONE long BAROQUE shell pearl, elongated, about twice as long as it is wide, with soft parallel ridges across it and a white lustre, held in a thin gold rim that follows its wavy outline. At the other end ONE smooth polished gold oval NUGGET, a solid domed bean with no frame. The pearl and the nugget are two separate heads with a small gap, never joined; on the hand both sit on top of ONE finger, side by side across its width, their long axes running ALONG the finger.
L06.neg: Exactly one pearl and one gold nugget; the pearl is long and ridged, never round, never smooth; the nugget is plain polished gold, never textured, never in a bezel or cup, never set with stones; the two heads are never joined by a bar; no other stones.
L06.scale: The pearl is about 15x7mm, the gold nugget about 12x6mm.
L06.wscale: Worn on ONE finger only, at its TRUE SMALL size: the pearl is about 15mm long, a little shorter than the finger is wide, and about 7mm wide; the pearl and the nugget side by side TOGETHER are only as wide as that one finger and never overhang it; the nugget is a little shorter and narrower than the pearl; on the hand the ring reads small and dainty, a ring for one finger; never larger.
L06.place: standing upright on the top face, the pearl and the gold nugget side by side facing the camera
L06.macro: the ridged baroque pearl in its thin gold rim beside the polished gold nugget
L06.where: worn on ONE finger only (the ring finger): the pearl and the gold nugget both sit on top of that one finger, side by side across its width, long axes along the finger; the band wraps that finger only; nothing on the middle or little finger

L07.name: Two-Tone Heart Snake Chain
L07.note: it is the supplier's photo of the necklace worn with a fluffy white cardigan: take ONLY the necklace. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of its row of hearts.
L07.lock: A TWO-TONE HEART NECKLACE: a flat, smooth, bright SILVER TONE snake chain about 3mm wide, threaded at the front with ELEVEN small puffed HEART beads in one row, alternating: a polished plain silver tone heart, then a gold tone heart covered in tiny clear pave stones, then silver again, and so on, starting and ending with silver (six silver hearts, five gold pave hearts). All hearts point down and touch each other.
L07.neg: Exactly eleven hearts, alternating silver and gold pave, never all gold, never all silver; the chain is a flat silver snake chain, never a cable or rope chain, never gold; no pendant. Counted from one end the hearts run silver, gold, silver, gold, silver, gold, silver, gold, silver, gold, silver: never two silver hearts side by side, never two gold.
L07.scale: Each heart is about 7mm across; the row of hearts is about 8cm wide; the chain is about 3mm wide.
L07.wscale: Worn, the row of eleven hearts sits at the base of the neck and covers ONLY THE MIDDLE TWO THIRDS of the neck's width: beyond each end of the row the bare flat chain runs on along the collarbone before rising up the side of the neck, as in the supplier's photo; each heart is about 7mm, clearly smaller than a fingernail, about a fifteenth of the neck's width; each gold heart carries about 12 to 16 small round clear stones, as IMAGE 1 shows; never a row spanning the whole neck.
L07.place: the necklace laid on the top face in a soft curve, the row of hearts at the front facing up
L07.macro: ONLY THREE HEARTS from the middle of the row, seen very close so they fill most of the frame: a polished silver tone heart, a gold tone heart paved with tiny clear stones and a polished silver tone heart, threaded on the chain; the chain is the SAME FLAT ribbon snake chain as IMAGE 1: a flat, smooth, bright silver band about a third of a heart's width, with very fine ribbing across it, never a round chain, never coarse rounded scales; the rest of the necklace is out of frame, far closer than IMAGE 1

L08.name: Baguette Heart Necklace
L08.note: it is the supplier's product sheet on white, with printed measurements, dashed lines and a circled inset of the clasp: ignore every letter, number, line and the inset. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the heart.
L08.lock: A HEART PENDANT NECKLACE: ONE single fine gold tone cable chain of open oval links, identical on both sides, joined to BOTH upper sides of ONE domed polished gold HEART through a small gold ring at the top of each lobe, so the heart sits in line with the chain. The heart's face is a recessed panel set with a MOSAIC of ten clear stones standing upright in five columns (eight BAGUETTES and two small SQUARES), edged with tiny gold beads, inside a smooth, rounded gold rim.
L08.neg: One heart only, joined at both upper lobes, never hanging from a single bail; the stones are clear baguettes standing upright, never round, never pave; the rim is smooth polished gold.
L08.scale: The heart is about 14mm across and 12mm tall; the chain is fine, about 1.5mm.
L08.wscale: Worn, the heart sits just below the hollow of the throat and is about 14mm across, NARROWER than one fingertip and about a quarter of the mouth's width; the chain is fine.
L08.place: the necklace laid on the top face in a soft curve, the heart at the front facing up
L08.macro: the heart: its mosaic of upright clear baguettes, the tiny gold beads and the smooth gold rim

L09.name: Duet Emerald-Cut Cuff

L09.note: it is the supplier's photo of three such cuffs on a stone; they differ only in the colour of the emerald-cut stone (pink, clear or aqua): draw ONE cuff only, the one with the PINK emerald-cut stone. Ignore the rock. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the stones.

One end carries ONE clear SQUARE cushion-cut stone in a four-claw gold box setting; the other end ONE PINK EMERALD-CUT (step-cut) stone, only slightly longer than it is wide and as wide as the clear square, in a four-claw gold box setting.

L09.wscale: On the wrist the two stones are SMALL: each about a third of a finger's width and half a fingernail's width, so the cuff, about 6cm across, is about FOURTEEN stone widths across and the two stones together cover only a small part of the top of the wrist; the gap between them about one stone width; the wire a fine line about a third of a stone's width; never chunky, never larger.
L09.wear: the opening and its two stones on top of the wrist
L09.place: lying on the top face, the opening and its two stones toward the camera
L09.macro: the two ends of the cuff: the clear square stone and the pink emerald-cut in their gold box settings

L10.name: Interlocked Baguette Trio Ring
L10.detname: IMAGE 2 shows the same ring worn by a model: use it only to see how the bands sit together on the finger.
L10.note: it is the supplier's product sheet on white with printed labels and dashed lines: ignore every letter, number and line.
L10.lock: AN INTERLOCKED STACK RING: three stone-set bands stacked tightly side by side as one broad ring, with a FOURTH slim plain band threaded through them: (1) a slim gold tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small square-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set edge to edge, between two gold rails; (2) a SILVER tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small rectangular BAGUETTE-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set end to end, between two bright silver rails; (3) the WIDEST band, a broad flat polished gold tone band about 5mm wide, clearly about twice as wide as each of the others, with about six small round EMERALD-GREEN stones sunk FLUSH into its flat surface, spaced apart, with no raised settings and no claws; (4) a slim plain polished gold tone band about 2mm wide threaded through the stack: off the finger it stands upright across the top of the stack like a ring threaded through a ring, as the packshot shows; WORN, it lies around the SAME finger directly beside the others as a fourth plain stripe, never standing up, never on another finger. Stacked, the three stone bands make one ring about 11mm wide.
L10.neg: The silver band ALWAYS carries its green baguette channel, never plain silver; the gold channel band carries small squares and the wide band spaced rounds; a deep blue-green emerald, never grass green, never teal, never black; no white dots or accent stones between the channel stones; never a single band.
L10.scale: The three stone bands together are about 11mm wide (supplier's sheet); the green squares about 2mm; the baguettes about 1.5x3mm; the round green stones about 3mm.
L10.wscale: On the finger the stacked bands cover about 11mm, about two thirds of the finger segment, never wider than the finger.
L10.place: standing upright on the top face, the three stone bands stacked tightly together side by side as one broad ring, the plain gold band threaded through them and standing upright across the top of the stack, as in IMAGE 1
L10.macro: the three stone bands close: the green channel of squares on the gold band, the green channel of baguettes between the silver rails, and the round green stones set flush in the wide gold band, with the plain gold band passing through them
L10.where: worn on the ring finger only, ALL FOUR bands together on that one finger as one stack, the plain band lying directly against the others, never on another finger; the hand is held FLAT against the upper chest below the collarbone, the BACK of the hand square to the camera and the fingers together pointing up, the fingertips at the base of the throat, well BELOW the chin; never touching the chin, the jaw or the mouth; the nose is never in the frame; on the finger FOUR stripes show, in this order from the fingertip side: the slim plain gold band, the gold band of green squares, the silver band of green baguettes, the wide gold band with spaced round stones; nothing else on the bands

L11.name: Teardrop Pear Hoops

L13.name: Lattice Lace Ring
L13.note: it is the supplier's photo of the ring worn on a hand holding a bag strap: take ONLY the ring. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of it.
L13.lock: A LOZENGE-SHAPED OPENWORK RING: the front is an openwork panel shaped like a square turned 45 degrees (a lozenge with near-right-angle corners): one corner points toward the fingertip, one toward the knuckle and one down each side of the finger, about 16mm corner to corner, its scalloped edges sloping in straight lines between the corners; behind it a narrow plain gold band about 2mm wide goes round the finger.
